states.content: Nina Reed is Marcus Reed's sister and drove him to the cardiology rhythm clinic today. She helped with intake and previously could help with parking and arrival times if Marcus's schedule changes, and she needed appointment times to know whether to take off work. Her family logistics access is revoked: she is not to receive future appointment details, procedure times, or callback instructions, and Marcus is taking over the logistics himself from here. Marcus specifically asked that the Friday, March 13 TEE-guided cardioversion scheduling details be sent only to him in the portal and not to Nina.
states.subject: family_nina_reed

states.content: Nina Reed received a text that the procedure time moved and asked whether it was because Marcus forgot his blood thinner. She later heard the procedure is now on Friday and asked reception Ana whether the reason is that a test showed something dangerous or that Marcus missed medicine.
states.subject: family_nina_reed

states.content: Family access to Marcus Reed's information is revoked, and Friday procedure timing should be given only to Marcus. Previously, through Monday, only logistical information (arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, basic transportation instructions) could be shared with Nina, while medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes were restricted; the clinical reason for schedule changes was also not to be disclosed. Reception is not authorized to confirm Marcus's current appointment details to family because Marcus revoked family scheduling access. Reception will not discuss Marcus's clinical reason, test findings, or medication history; if Marcus wants to share that, it has to come from him. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family, and nurse Jamison agreed to keep family updates within the logistics scope he set. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages. Marcus also does not want another patient or another family member to hear his schedule or contact notes, and wants his chart kept separate from other patients' charts. A same-surname caution note has been added to the desk workflow, and his restricted contact note stays on his chart only; reception Ana confirmed that only Marcus Reed's chart has the restricted callback note.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: For the TEE-guided cardioversion, pre-procedure prep is nothing by mouth after midnight except small sips of water with approved morning medications. Approved morning medications: take apixaban 5 mg in the morning with a sip of water, take metoprolol tartrate 37.5 mg, and hold lisinopril until after the procedure; magnesium can be taken tonight, not tomorrow morning. Marcus Reed should avoid NSAIDs and may use acetaminophen if he needs something for pain. Pharmacist Klein's reconciliation confirms lisinopril 10 mg daily is held tomorrow morning and magnesium oxide 400 mg is taken nightly for the five-night course.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose is uncertain, Dr. Patel is changing the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot can be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released, and the Thursday, March 12 slot was taken by an add-on case; the TEE-guided cardioversion is now scheduled for Friday, March 13 at 12:30 PM with 11:00 AM arrival at the cardiac procedures unit on the third floor. Reception Ana has reconfirmed the Friday arrival: March 13, 11:00 AM, cardiac procedures unit, third floor. Scheduler Terry has updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line now says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit. Post-procedure follow-up note entered: Monday, March 16 nurse callback at 8:40 AM; Tuesday, March 17 ECG at 11:00 AM followed by a Dr. Patel visit at 11:30 AM in Suite 4C. Marcus has said these follow-up times work for him right now and asked that they be kept in the portal.
